chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he used to say:

The one who clothes a believer with a garment from his bareness, Allah will clothe him from the brocades of Paradise; and the one who clothes a believer with a garment from his adequacy, will not cease to be in a veil from Allah for as long as there remains a rag from the cloth.

key_terms.إِسْتَبَقُ: Fine silk or brocade, a type of high-quality garment
key_terms.خِرْقَةٌ: A rag, piece of cloth, or remnant
key_terms.عُرْيٍ: Bareness, nakedness, or lack of clothing

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for clothing a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this tradition from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing that clothing a believer is an act of spiritual protection (satr) that mirrors divine mercy. The hadith distinguishes between relieving basic nakedness, which earns the reward of wearing istabraq (silk of Paradise), and enhancing the attire of the clothed, which ensures continuous divine covering as long as the garment remains. This reflects the Shia emphasis on social solidarity and the tangible spiritual rewards of material generosity within the community of believers.
